8. Field strategies with sub-activities
(a) Stepping up protection: (antipoaching squad/Tiger Protection Force deployment)
The antipoaching operations in Tiger Reserves are site specific. However, the following
activities, inter alia , would form part of the protection strategy in Tiger Reserves:
• Raising, arming and deployment of Special Tiger Protection Force.
• Use of information technology in wildlife crime prevention.
• Launching M-STrIPES for field patrolling.
• Deployment of antipoaching squads.
• Establishing and maintenance of existing patrolling camps/chowkis and deployment of
camp labourers for patrolling.
• Organising vehicular patrolling by constituting squads (Tiger Protection Force),
comprising of field staff, labourers and police/SAF/ex-army personnel, with wireless
handset and paraphernalia for apprehending offenders, apart from prescribing a
patrolling calendar for the squad.
• Establishing and maintenance of wireless network.

45
• Organising surprise raids jointly with the local police in railway stations, local trains,
bus-stops, buses, catchers and cafeteria.
• Ensuring special site-specific protection measures, during monsoon as ‘Operation
Monsoon’ – considering the terrain and accessibility of Protected Areas.
• Deployment of ex-army personnel/home guards.
• Deployment of local work force for patrolling, surveillance of water holes, manning
barriers.
• Procurement of arms and ammunition.
• Procurement/maintenance of elephant squads.
• Rewards to informers.
• Legal support for defending court cases.
• Procurement of vehicles, boats.
• Procurement field gear, night vision device.
(b) Deciding inviolate spaces for wildlife and relocation of villagers from core or critical
tiger habitats in Tiger Reserves within a timeframe and settlement of rights:
The Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972, as well as the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional
Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006, require that rights of people (Scheduled
Tribes and other traditional forest dwellers) recognized in forest areas within core/critical tiger/wildlife
habitats of tiger reserves/protected areas may be modified and resettled for providing inviolate spaces
to tiger/wild animals. This requires payment of compensation (rights settlement in addition to the
relocation package offered under the CSS at present). Chapter IV of the Wild Life (Protection) Act,
1972 (Section 24) provides for acquisition of rights in or over the land declared by the State
Government under Section 18 (for constituting a Sanctuary) or Section 35 (for constituting a National
Park). Sub-section 2 of Section 24 of the Wild Life (Protection) Act, authorizes the Collector to
acquire such land or rights. Therefore, payment of compensation for the immovable property of
people forms part of modifying/settling their rights which is a statutory requirement.
The ongoing study and the analysis of the available research data on tiger ecology indicate
that the minimum population of tigresses in breeding age, which are needed to maintain a viable
population of 80-100 tigers (in and around core) require an inviolate space of 800-1200 sq. km.
Tiger being an “umbrella species”, this will also ensure viable populations of other wild animals
(co-predators, prey) and forest, thereby ensuring the ecological viability of the entire area/habitat.
Thus, it becomes an ecological imperative to keep the core areas of tiger reserves inviolate for the
survival of source populations of tiger and other wild animals.
The proposed package has two options:
Option I – Payment of the entire package amount (Rs. 10 lakhs per family) to the family
in case the family opts so, without involving any rehabilitation/relocation process by the
Forest Department.
Option II – Carrying out relocation/rehabilitation of village from protected area/tiger reserve
by the Forest Department.
(c) Strengthening of infrastructure within Tiger Reserves:
The following activities, inter alia , would form part of reinforcing the infrastructure of
Tiger Reserves (including support to new tiger reserves):

46
• Civil Works (staff quarters, family hostels, office improvement, patrolling camp, house
keeping buildings, museum, culverts).
• Maintenance/creation/upgradation of road network.
• Maintenance/creation of wireless tower.
• Maintenance/creation of fire watch tower.
• Maintenance/creation of bridges, dams, anicuts.
• Maintenance/creation of firelines/firebreaks.
• Maintenance/creation of earthen ponds.
• Procurement/maintenance of vehicles (Gypsy, Jeep, Truck, Tractor).
• Habitat improvement works.
• Procurement of hardware, software/GIS.
• Procurement of compass, range finder, GPS, camera traps.
• Procurement of satellite imageries for management planning.
• Map digitization facility for management planning.
(d) Habitat improvement and water development:
These, inter alia , may include:  weed eradication, removal of gregarious plant growth from
grasslands, grass improvement, water retention structures and the like. These initiatives would
increase the forage and browse values of the habitat for wild animals.
(e) Addressing man-animal conflict (ensuring uniform, timely compensation for human
deaths due to wild animals, livestock depredation by carnivores, crop depredation by wild
ungulates) (compensation for crop loss is a new component):
This would involve:
• Payment of compensation for cattle lifting, death of human beings and crop
depredation due to wild animals.
• Creation of crop protection structures.
• Procurement/deployment of traps, cages to catch problematic animals.
• Procurement of tranquilizing equipments, rescue vehicles and drugs.
(f) Co-existence agenda in buffer/fringe areas:
The fringe areas around Tiger Reserve have corridor value, and their ecological
sustainability is important to prevent the area from becoming ecological sinks on account of over
use of resources and unwise land use. This calls for delineation of buffer zone around a tiger
reserve to incorporate such fringe areas so that it can fulfill the following objectives:
• Providing ecologically viable livelihood options to local stakeholders for reducing their
dependency on forests.
• Conserving the forest area through restorative inputs involving local people for
providing habitat supplement to wild animals moving out of core areas.

47
(g) Rehabilitation of traditional hunting tribes living around tiger reserves:
There is an urgent need to launch a rehabilitation and development programme for the
denotified tribes and tribes involved in traditional hunting, living around tiger reserves and tiger
corridors. The following denotified tribes/communities are involved in traditional hunting of wild
animals : Behelias, Ambalgars, Badaks, Mongias, Bavariyas, Monglias, Pardhi, Boyas, Kaikads,
Karwal Nat, Nirshikaris, Picharis, Valayaras, Yenadis, Chakma, Mizo, Bru, Solung and Nyishi. While
this list is not exhaustive, around 5,000 such families are required to be taken up under a welfare
programme (forming part of NTCA initiatives) during the Plan period. The rehabilitation/welfare
package should be evolved in a site specific, consultative manner with livelihood options, to include :
wages for such people towards their deployment in foot patrolling for protecting wildlife, providing
agricultural land with irrigation, basic health care, housing and related community welfare inputs
and basic education facilities. The experience gained in the past for settling denotified tribes by the
salvation army is required to be considered dispassionately while structuring the programme.
(h) Research and field equipments:
The All India tiger estimation using the new methodology approved by the Tiger task Force
has resulted in a permanent monitoring protocol for the field units. The Phase-IV tiger reserve level
would be launched to monitor the source populations of tiger. Further, assistance would be
provided for fostering field oriented research and to equip the staff with facilities like GPS, camera
traps, night vision, range finder and related accessories including hardware and software.
(i) Staff development and capacity building:
This would involve:
• Capacity building/training.
• Providing project allowance and special incentives.
• Specialized training in the use of GIS, antipoaching operations.
• Specialized training in jurisprudence and wildlife forensics.
• Study tours for appraisal of good practices in other reserves.
• Dissemination workshops.
• Specialized training in park interpretation.
• Specialized training in management planning.
The above inputs are extremely important for enhancing the skill of field staff. Several
instances of poaching occur for want of specialized training in crime detection and related skills.
(j) Mainstreaming wildlife concerns in tiger bearing forests and fostering corridor
conservation through restorative strategy involving locals to arrest fragmentation of
habitats:
This would involve:
• Redressing man-animal conflict.
• Capturing problematic/aberrant wild animals.
• Monitoring of wild animals.
• Antipoaching operations.
• Habitat improvement measures.

48
(k) Safeguards/Retrofitting measures in the interest of wildlife conservation:
Several Tiger Reserves are affected on account of heavily used infrastructure like roads, railway
tracks and others. The high tension electric lines passing through many reserves cause mortality of wild
animals due to electrocution by poachers. In the interest of wild animals several safeguards as well as
retrofitting measures may be required, which would be supported on a site-specific basis.
(l) Providing basic infrastructure/Project Tiger Headquarter expenditure for consultancy,
all India tiger estimation/continuous monitoring of tigers outside tiger reserves,
strengthening of NTCA at the Center. The following are envisaged:
• Creation of office space at Delhi for National Tiger Conservation Authority.
• Carrying out All India Tiger Estimation, monitoring.
• Support to research work.
• Contractual arrangement for special studies.
• International/National Workshops.
• Contractual arrangement for data entry, analysis.
(m) Independent monitoring and evaluation of tiger reserves:
The second round of independent monitoring has been completed using globally accepted
indicators. This would be further refined and continued.
(n) Establishment and development of new Tiger Reserves:
‘Project Tiger’ has a holistic ecosystem approach. Though the focus is on the flagship
species ‘tiger’, the project strives to maintain the stability of ecosystem by fostering other trophic
levels in the food chain. This is essential to ensure an ecologically viable population of tiger, which
is at the ‘apex’ of the ecological food chain. The community pressures on forests are ever on the
increase in developing countries, and India is no exception. As a sequel, the tiger habitat has
become fragile and weak at several places, warranting a focused conservation approach. Our
protected areas/Tiger Reserves are analogous to “islands” in an ocean of the other-use patterns.
Empirical evidences from ‘island biogeography’ indicate that “isolated” reserves lose their species
rapidly owing to ‘ecological insularization’. Further, apart from fragmentation, the situation is
aggravated by degraded forest cover owing to biotic pressure, dislocated prey – predator ratio,
absence of effective measures to ensure the desired level of protection and lack of eco
developmental initiatives for the fringe dwelling stake holders to reduce their dependency on forest
resources. Since ‘Project Tiger’ would go a long way in redressing the above situation, the
Steering Committee of Project Tiger in its meeting held on 23.1.2003 recommended inclusion of
new Tiger Reserve areas so as to increase the total area of Project Tiger from existing 37761 sq.
kms. to 50,000 sq. kms. during the Tenth Plan period.
(o) Provision of Project Allowance to staff of Project Tiger:
The tiger States would be supported (100%) for Project Allowance to staff of Tiger
Reserves.
(p) Staff welfare activities:
Staff welfare inputs like residential accommodation for the children of frontline staff in
nearby towns/villages, supply of kerosene, medicine, field kit, mosquito net, torch and the like
would be supported.

49
(q) Fostering Eco-Tourism in Tiger Reserves:
‘Ecotourism’ in the context of Tiger Reserves is ecologically sustainable nature-tourism,
which is emerging as an important component of tourism industry. It is distinct from ‘mass
tourism’, having sustainable, equitable, community based effort for improving the living standards
of local, host communities living on the fringes of Tiger Reserves. Ecotourism is proposed to
be fostered with financial support to the host community through ‘soft loans’ from
Ecodevelopment Committees, in accordance with site – specific ‘Ecotourism plan’ and carrying
capacity of Tiger Reserves in the buffer areas. The core/critical tiger habitats would not be used
for any form of tourism, and the ongoing tourism activities in such areas should be phased out
in the fringe/buffer areas, without affecting its corridor value. The development of tourism
related facilities within the buffer zones of Tiger Reserves would continue with inputs under
Project Tiger. The opportunities for stakeholders would include management of low cost
accommodation for tourists, providing guide services, providing sale outlets, managing
excursions, organizing ethnic dances and the like.

1
REPORT
The Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Department of Space on
the recommendations contained in the Two Hundred and Twenty Fifth Report of the Department-
related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Science and Technology, Environment and Forests on
the Demands for Grants (2012-13) of the Department of Space, which was presented to both the
Houses of Parliament on 18
th May, 2012. There were fifteen recommendations in the Two Hundred
and Twenty Fifth Report of the Committee. Action Taken notes on the recommendations of the
Committee were received from the Department on 5 th September, 2012.
The Committee’s recommendations, action taken thereon and comments of the Committee
on the Action Taken by the Department of Space are set out in the succeeding paragraphs.
MONITORING MECHANISM FOR ONGOING SCHEMES
Recommendation (Para 5.3)
The Committee is of the view that an effective monitoring mechanism is vital to ensure that
the various projects are completed as per the schedule and there is no time or cost overruns. In
this context, the Committee appreciates the adoption of the Result Framework Document (RFD)
by the Department, which aims towards an effective appraisal of the actual physical and financial
progress/achievements in implementation of policies/programmes in comparison to the projected
targets for each programme. The Committee, in view of strengthening of monitoring mechanism,
hopes that the Department would, in future, be able to ensure timely completion of projects and
optimum utilization of funds.
Action Taken by Government
The views of the Committee are noted. The Department will continue to put an effort to
ensure timely completion of projects with optimum utilization of funds.
Comments
The Committee hopes that the Department will make a critical review of its
monitoring mechanism and plug the gaps, wherever necessary, so as to preclude any scope
of time and cost overruns.
ELEVENTH PLAN ACHIEVEMENTS AND TWELFTH FIVE YEAR PLAN
Recommendation (Para 6.2)
The Committee appreciates the achievements made by the Department during the Eleventh
Plan, notably the Chandrayaan-1 Mission and progress made in the field of Launch Vehicle
Development, Earth Observation and Satellite Communication Systems. However, it notes with
concern that some of the missions such as Radar Imaging Satellite (RISAT-1), Advanced
Meteorological satellite INSAT-3D, Multi-wavelength X-ray astronomy satellites ASTROSAT,
SARAL, GSAT-9, GSAT-10, GSAT-6/6A, GSAT-11 and IRNSS could not be completed as per
schedule and shall spill over to the Twelfth Plan period due to technological developmental
complexities, difficulties in sourcing the critical supplies and mission contingencies. The Committee
hopes Department would make all possible efforts to tide over these difficulties and projects would
be completed as per the revised schedule.

2
Action Taken by Government
Noted. It is brought to the notice of the Committee that Radar Imaging Satellite (RISAT-1)
has already been launched on 26 th April, 2012. GSAT-10 satellite is scheduled to be launched in
September, 2012. As recommended by the committee, the Department will make all possible efforts
to complete the remaining spill-over missions as per the revised schedule.
Comments
The Committee congratulates the Department on the successful launch of the RISAT-
I and hopes that the Department will make all out efforts to launch its remaining spill-over
missions during the Twelfth Plan period.
Recommendation (Para 6.5 and 6.6)
The Committee notes that in the Twelfth Five Year Plan (2012-17) the major thrust of the
Indian Space programme will be to carry forward and strengthen the already established space based
services aimed at socio-economic development of the country. The Committee hopes that, apart from
the ongoing space programmes and its efforts for developing advanced launch vehicles, the
Department should also strive for mastering critical technologies, so as to reduce the chances of
failure of important missions. The Committee is of the opinion that the next stepping stone of the
Department should be to strive towards sending a Manned Mission to Space, which naturally follows
from its successes obtained in sending launch vehicles which can carry higher payloads to space.
Action Taken by Government
Noted. Department has taken up activities for development of critical technologies required
for the advanced missions such as Re-usable Launch V ehicles, Manned Spaceflight, advanced
communication satellite, sub-meter resolution remote sensing satellites and planetary exploration.
The Department is also actively pursuing the development of the heavy lift launch vehicle, the
GSLV-MkIII.
Recommendation (Para 6.6)
The Committee also recommends that Department should also strive to increase its global
market share in space services by developing more innovative and competitive space services on
commercial lines and the revenue generated from marketing of these services, should be used for
further growth and development of space technology in the country. This will also increasingly
reduce the dependence of our space programme on budgetary resources.
Action Taken by Government
Noted. Department is pursuing the commercial activities through Antrix Corporation Limited.
Space Services in the global market is provided by Antrix in the areas of Remote Sensing Data,
Value Added Services, Communication Transponders, design and development of custom-built
satellite, PSLV Launch Services and Ground Station Services. The Annual Revenue of Antrix has
grown from Rs. 940.26 crores in 2007-08 to Rs. 1179.92 crores (provisional) in 2011-12. Antrix
has plans to further expand its activities to increase its share in space services in the global market
in the coming years.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply of the Department and hopes that Antrix would be
able to secure a respectable share in global market in space services in the near future.

3
MANNED MISSION INITIATIVE
Recommendation (Para 8.3)
The Committee notes with concern that a programme initiated in the year 2006 and having
target date of 2014 as its completion, is yet to get a final approval even for its Phase 1
programme. It shows that the Department is either not serious in timely completion of the project
or has casually fixed a schedule for its completion. It also reflects a lack of proper planning and
effective monitoring, as also absence of adequate research and technological support for timely
execution of the project. The Committee, however hopes that the pre-project activities would be
expeditiously completed and approval for Phase 1 of the programme obtained, so that the project
is completed as per schedule in the year 2014.
Action Taken by Government
Noted. After a careful consideration of the magnitude of efforts, investments and
technological complexities involving development of a host of new technologies in diverse areas,
it was decided to take up the Manned Mission Programme in a phased manner focusing on the
development of critical technologies in the initial phase. Accordingly, the pre-project activities in the
areas of Crew module development, Environmental Control and Life Support System etc. are
progressing satisfactorily.
Comments
The Committee finds that the Department in its reply has  neither advanced any
reason for the delay nor underlined the efforts made by them to complete its pre-project
activities. The Committee,  therefore, reiterates that the pre-project activities for the
mission may be completed within a fixed time-frame.
CHANDRAYAAN-2 AND MARS ORBITER MISSION
Recommendation (Para 9.5)
The Committee after going thoroughly through the aforesaid reply of the Department is of
the opinion that preparation of an optimistic schedule for missions like Chandrayaan-2 and Mars
Orbiter Mission, alone is not sufficient but what is required is the will and dedication to complete
the mission target within the time schedule. If time schedule does not inspire the confidence of
the team and is seen by it as an unrealistic target, it will hardly serve any purpose. The Department
should therefore, fix time schedules in a more realistic way, rather than fixing time schedules
which are not to be adhered. The Committee feels that failure to adhere to programme schedule
sends a wrong message to the public and lowers their confidence in our capability to take our
space programme to new heights. The Committee, therefore, strongly recommends that the
schedule for all missions including complex missions should be prepared only after taking into
account all ground realities, so that a realistic schedule meant to be adhered by all, rather than that
being violated with impunity, is prepared.
Action Taken by Government
Noted. Department prepares schedules for the project taking into account the development
time required for the key/new technologies and the lead time required for fabrication, assembly,
integration and testing activities. The Department has also implemented a Project Management
Structure involving multi-level periodical reviews of the project progress to ensure that the projects

4
are realized within the targeted schedule. Chandrayaan-2 was approved in September, 2008 as an
Indo-Russian joint mission with an objective of carrying out in-situ Lunar surface studies using
Moon Lander and Rover. Russia had the responsibility of developing the ‘Moon Lander and Rover’,
while India had the responsibility of developing the ‘Moon Orbiter’ and launch by Geo-synchronous
Satellite Launch Vehicle (GSLV).
However, based on the suggestion from Russian side, technical configuration of
Chandrayaan-2 mission was revised in February 2010. As per the revised plan, Russia took the
responsibility to realize the ‘Moon Lander’ and ISRO took up the responsibility to realize the Rover
and module.
Subsequent to the failure of the Russian interplanetary mission Phobos-Grunt, Russian side
has proposed for a shift in approach for Chandrayaan-2 mission in a recent meeting held at
Bangalore on May 12, 2012. As per the communication, Russia wants to increase the reliability of
their planetary missions by incorporating additional redundant systems. As a result, the mass of the
proposed ‘Moon Lander’ is likely to increase and the Lander will be made available only during
2014. These recent inputs from Russia have called for a programmatic realignment for
Chandrayaan-2 mission which is being examined by the Department. However, the Department
would continue to strive hard and spare no efforts in meeting the project time schedules.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
INDIAN INSTITUTE OF SPACE SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
Recommendation (Para 10.3)
The Committee commends the initiative of the Department in setting up of the Indian
Institute of Space Science and Technology (IIST) for developing high quality man power required
for our space programmes and research. The Committee is further happy to note that it is Asia’s
first Space Institute to offer the complete range of courses related to space sciences. The
Committee hopes that the Institute would turn into a centre of excellence imparting high quality
space education and producing highly skilled and proficient space scientists and technologists. The
Committee is happy to note that a large numbers of students are competing for admission to the
IIST, which indicates growing popularity and importance of the institute.
Action Taken by the Government
Noted. From the current academic year, the institute has started four Post Graduation
programmes in the areas of RF and Microwave Engineering, Aerospace Propulsion Engineering,
Optical-Engineering and Digital Signal Processing. Moreover, the Institute is offering doctoral
programme in various areas of research which are relevant to Space and advanced technology areas
which would enable IIST to become a centre of excellence.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply of the Department.
OCEANSAT AND RESOURCESAT PROGRAMMES
Recommendation (Para 11.5)
The Committee observes that for both the Oceansat 2 and 3 and Resourcesat 2 and 3

5
programmes, there has been a trend to seek substantial budgetary allocations at B.E. stage without
making an extensive and critical assessment of the actual requirements. The Committee feels that
budgetary demands should be sought by the Department only after comprehensive analysis of the
actual fund requirement for the programme. Scarce resources should not be blocked by asking for
ambitious allocations and not utilizing them subsequently. These instances are also a reflection on
the capacity of the Department to plan its projects, efficiently, set realistic targets and its
determination to achieve the targets set.
Action Taken by Government
Noted.
Comments
The Committee expresses its displeasure that the Department has not initiated any
action in pursuance of the observations of the Committee and has simply noted it. The
Committee hopes that the Department would, in future, make extensive and critical
assessments of its actual requirements.
TELE-MEDICINE
Recommendation (Para 12.4)
The Committee feels that Telemedicine is a very useful programme pursued by the
Department for providing societal benefits by use of space technology to the common masses. The
Committee is aware that to provide even the basic healthcare facilities in all the villages of the
country, would require a huge capital investment, both in terms of manpower and resources. The
Committee is, therefore, of the opinion that this is a very cost effective method for providing
quality healthcare facilities in the rural and remote areas of the country. The Committee
recommends that the telemedicine network should be expanded in a time-bound manner to cover
the backward, remote, inaccessible or disease-prone areas, left out so far.
Action Taken by Government
Noted. Since 2001, ISRO has been providing Telemedicine nodes in a phased manner. It
covers remote regions of the country including J&K, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Lakshadweep
islands and most of the mainland States.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply of the Department and presumes that the
Department will spread their telemedicine programme over to other left out places soon.
Recommendation (Para 12.5)
The Committee also notes that due to the failure of the launch vehicle carrying the
GSAT-5P satellite, the expansion of telemedicine network work was adversely affected. The
Committee is happy to note that with the successful launch of GSAT-12, the telemedicine activities
are being restored. The Committee hopes that the migration of telemedicine network to GSAT-12
satellite, which is currently in progress, will be completed soon and the expansion of the facility
will be pursued with vigour.

6
Action Taken by Government
Noted. Two transponders in GSAT-12 satellite are allotted by INSAT Coordination
Committee (ICC) for tele-medicine programme. Out of 382 tele-medicine nodes, 190 tele-
medicine nodes were planned to be migrated to GSAT-12 satellite and rest of the nodes are to
be operated through INSAT-3A, INSAT-3C and INSAT-4A satellites. Against the 190 nodes that
are scheduled for migration, 165 nodes have already been migrated and actions are taken to
migrate the remaining nodes. In order to ensure the effective utilization of all the tele-medicine
nodes, steps are taken up by DOS/ISRO to enter into an appropriate maintenance agreements and
for monitoring activities.
Comments
The Committee applauds the Department for migration of 165 nodes out of 190 and
hopes that the migration of the remaining nodes would be done soon.
DISASTER MANAGEMENT SUPPORT SYSTEM
Recommendation (Para 13.3)
The Committee is of the view that natural disasters such as floods, droughts, cyclones,
earthquakes and landslides are a recurring phenomena and every year widespread economic
devastation and loss of human lives is caused on account of these natural calamities. The
Committee is of the opinion that the services of Virtual Private Network (VPN) which has been
set up for networking the State and district level emergency control centres for natural disasters
management must be optimally utilized for rapid dissemination of information to lessen the human
and economic loss.
Action Taken by Government
Noted. Presently, the satellite based Virtual Private Network set up under the Disaster
Management Support (DMS) Programme offers connectivity to the following:
(i) 20 State Emergency Operation centres (Andhra Pradesh, Andaman and Nicobar
Islands, Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Bihar, Delhi, Gujarat, Himachal Pradesh, Kerala,
Maharashtra, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland and Orissa, Sikkim, Tamil
Nadu, Tripura, Uttarakhand, and West Bengal)
(ii) 5 observation nodes (Prime Minister Office, Prime Minister residence, National
Disaster Management Authority, Delhi, Cabinet Secretariat, Delhi, and Control Room
North Block)
(iii) 10 primary nodes (National Remote sensing Centre, Hyderabad, National Remote
Sensing Centre, Shadnagar, Indian Meteorological Department, Central Water
Commission, Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services, Geologlcal
Survey of India, New Delhi, Space Application Centre, Ahmedabad; NESAC, Shillong;
Master Control Facility, Hassan and National Institute of Disaster Management, Delhi)
The Virtual Private Network which was earlier functional through INSAT-3E satellite is re-
established to its full capacity by allotting a full transponder in GSAT-12 and all the nodes are now
re-aligned with GSAT-12. To further optimize the usage of the network, periodical meetings of the
nodal officers from the States and the data providing nodes will be organized.

7
Comments
The Committee is happy to hear that Virtual Private Network (VPN) has been re-
established to its full capacity by allotting a full transponder in GSAT-12 and reiterates that
efforts may be made to link State and district level emergency control centres through VPN.
SPACE INDUSTRY PARTNERSHIP
Recommendation (Para 14.3)
The Committee is of the opinion that active involvement and effective participation of more
and more Indian industries in providing quality products and services needed for our Space
programme will lead to self-reliance and would decrease our dependence on foreign industries for
space equipments and technologies. The involvement of Indian industries in production of
aggregates/systems for the Indian Space programme would augment the technical expertise of the
Indian industry and would also lead to employment generation. The Committee, therefore,
recommends that the Department of Space should make concerted efforts in this direction. The
Committee also desires that Department of Space should look forward to transfer more and more
technologies which may be useful for civilian applications to Indian Industries so as to make them
globally competitive.
Action Taken by Government
Noted. Department has been progressively increasing the participation of Indian Industries
in the Space Programme. The focus has been to upgrade the Indian Industries from mere supplier
of parts/components/subsystem to system level integrator. The Indian Industries are also supported
with transfer of ISRO developed technologies to make them globally competitive.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
FAILURE ANALYSIS COMMITTEE (FAC)
Recommendation (Para 15.4)
After going through the replies of the Department of Space and findings of FAC, the
Committee is of the opinion that the Department should make efforts to develop our indigenous
cryogenic engines for GSLV and other advanced launch vehicles, as it would make us self reliant
in this important area. The Committee would however like the Department to ensure that every
possible care is taken while launching our satellite so that chances of failure are reduced to the
minimum. It should bear in mind that any failure of our missions, though failures are bound to
happen in such complex missions, not only results in loss of crores of rupees but also raises a
doubt in the mind of the people about the credibility of our space programme.
Action Taken by Government
Noted. Development of indigenous cryogenic engines for GSLV is a critical milestone for
making India’s launch vehicle programme self-reliant. Hence the development of indigenous
cryogenic is being taken up on priority basis. The recommendations of Failure Analysis Committees
(FAC) have been implemented in the realization of the indigenous cryogenic upper stage for the
next development flight of GSLV , i.e., GSLV-D5.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.

MINUTES

10

11

nd to 238 th Reports on

PREFACE
I, the Chairman of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Science
and Technology, Environment and Forests, having been authorised by the Committee to present the
Report on its behalf, present this Two Hundred Thirty Sixth Report on the Action Taken by the
Ministry of Earth Sciences on the recommendations contained in Two Hundred Twenty Sixth
Report of the Committee on Demands for Grants (2012-2013) of the Ministry of Earth Sciences.
2. The Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Ministry of Earth Sciences
on the recommendations contained in the Two Hundred Twenty Sixth Report of the Department-
related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Science and Technology, Environment and Forests on
the Demands for Grants (2012-2013) of the Ministry of Earth Sciences which was presented to
the Rajya Sabha on 18
th May, 2012.
3. There were twenty two recommendations contained in the Two Hundred Twenty Sixth
Report of the Committee. Action Taken Notes on the recommendations of the Committee were
received from the Ministry on 27
th July, 2012.
4. In the meeting held on 17 th December, 2012, the Committee considered the Draft Action
Taken Report and adopted the same.
DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY

1
REPORT
The Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Ministry of Earth Sciences
on the recommendations contained in the Two Hundred Twenty-sixth Report of the Department-
related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Science and Technology, Environment and Forests on
the Demands for Grants (2012-2013) of the Ministry of Earth Sciences, which was presented to
both the Houses of Parliament on 18
th May, 2012. There were twenty-two recommendations in the
Report of the Committee. Action Taken notes on the recommendations of the Committee were
received from the Department on 27
th July, 2012.
The Committee’s recommendations, action taken thereon and comments of the Committee
on the action taken by the Ministry of Earth Sciences are set out in the succeeding paragraphs:-
Recommendation (Para 5.3)
The Committee feels that without any financial and administrative powers, the Earth
Commission will hardly be effective in performing its role and functions and the very purpose of
setting up of Earth Commission would be defeated. The Committee, therefore, recommends that
immediate steps be taken to provide necessary financial and administrative powers to the Earth
Commission so that it may carry out its assigned role effectively.
Action Taken by Government
Expressing the gratitude to the Committee for supporting the proposal on administrative and
financial support to Earth Commission, the Ministry would like to apprise the Committee that a
draft Cabinet Note of the proposal on administrative and financial powers to the Earth Commission
has already been circulated to all the concerned Ministries/agencies. Currently, their comments on
the same being obtained from the concerned Ministries.
Comments
The Committee hopes that the comments of the concerned Ministries/agencies would have
been received by now and a decision taken. The Committee reiterates its view that administrative
and financial powers be granted without any further delay to the Earth Commission.
Recommendation (Para 6.3)
The Committee notes with satisfaction that Result Framework Document (RFD), has been
adopted by the Ministry to review and monitor physical and financial progress/achievements of
major activities with respect to agreed targets fixed for each programme, in addition to its internal
monitoring mechanisms. The Committee is of the opinion that an effective monitoring mechanism
is imperative for ensuring that the various projects are completed as per the projected schedule and
timely action taken to overcome problems that may arise in the implementation of the projects. The
Committee hopes that with potent monitoring mechanisms, the Ministry would be able to complete
its projects in time.
Action Taken by Government
As pointed out by the Committee, the Ministry has adopted an adequate monitoring
mechanism (3-tier) to monitor the effective performance of various schemes towards timely

2
accomplishing the targets of the projects, including RFDs for all the centres of the Ministry. At
Ministry level, the Earth System Science Organisation (ESSO) Council set up by the Ministry meets
twice in a year to review in detail the performance of various programmes which are generally held
in April and September in the beginning of the financial year and middle of the year. Besides, the
performances of major projects are being monitored by Project Management and Advisory Council.
The progress of autonomous bodies of the Ministry is also monitored periodically by Finance
Committee, Governing Bodies and Research Advisory Committee, besides being monitored by the
Planning Commission on annual basis.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and hopes that effective monitoring would lead to
timely completion of projects.
Recommendation (Para 7.3)
In this connection the Committee would like to invite the attention of the Ministry to its
204
th Report (page 3, para 5.1) on the Demands for Grants (2010-11), wherein it has been stated
that as per information furnished by the Ministry, the total initial Budgetary allocation of Rs.7004.00
crores for the Eleventh five year Plan was revised to Rs.6637.00 crores at the mid term appraisal
stage. In comparison to this, the Committee has observed that the projected amount has been
increased by almost three times during Twelfth Plan with outlay proposed by the Ministry at
Rs.18,824.00 crores. The Committee also notes that for focused attention and securing effective
implementation, Ministry has reoriented its 76 projects into 15 major programmes for Twelfth Plan.
The Committee hopes that with increased allocations and more focused attention, the Ministry
would be able to achieve capacity for reliable weather forecasts at par with the highest international
standards and would be able to develop technologies needed for effective exploitation of marine
resources for the socio-economic development of our people during the Twelfth Plan period.
Action Taken by Government
The Ministry would like to assure that every effort would be made to achieve the targets
set for Twelfth Five Year Plan, in a more focused way. These included providing reliable weather
forecast at par with international standards, as the numerical weather forecast models, being
employed to develop these weather products by the Ministry, are similar to global models used by
the advanced countries. Besides, more local data collected from the autonomous platforms/sensors
would be assimilated into these models, which will enhance weather forecasting capability. Similarly
the various technology being developed by the Ministry to harness marine resources are the state-
of-the-art technology used elsewhere.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and is of the view that increased demand for budget
allocation, should be matched by proper utilization of funds on the part of the Ministry.
Recommendation (Para 7.4)
The Committee also notes that two projects viz. Multi-channel Seismic System on board
Sagar Kanya and National Institute of Ocean Technology (NIOT) extension centre in West Bengal,
could not be completed during the Eleventh Plan period. The Committee would like Ministry to
make all possible efforts to complete these programmes as soon as possible and well before the
expiry of the first year of the Twelfth Plan.

3
Action Taken by Government
It may kindly be noted that the above mentioned two projects have been dropped in
consultation with the Planning Commission. However, the objectives envisaged under the projects
could be pursued through existing ongoing programmes of the Ministry without jeopardizing the
goal of these projects.
Comments
The Committee expresses its concern that two of its projects pursued during the
Eleventh Five Year Plan have been dropped without assigning any reason. The Committee
hopes that as assured by the Ministry, the objectives envisaged under these projects would
be pursued through existing programmes of the Ministry.
Recommendation (Para 8.2)
The Committee observes that the Ministry has received a plan outlay of Rs.1281.00 crores,
which is Rs.369.00 crores less than the amount of Rs.1650.00 crores, projected by the Ministry.
The Committee, however, notes with surprise and concern that Twelfth Five Year Plan of the
Ministry is yet to be finalized and the Ministry is not certain about some of the new initiatives that
it had proposed during the Plan period. The Committee recommends that all possible efforts may
be made to finalise the Twelfth Five Year Plan of the Ministry at the earliest so that future roadmap
of the Ministry’s action Plan becomes certain and it can vigorously pursue the Plan targets and
achieve them.
Action Taken by Government
As recommended, finalization of Twelfth Five Year Plan proposals of the Ministry has been
completed and waiting for the final approval of the Planning Commission. Meanwhile the Ministry
has been actively engaged to seek the necessary approvals/clearances of the Government on various
Schemes proposed for implementation during Twelfth Plan.
Comments
The Committee hopes that the Ministry after obtaining the approval of the Planning
Commission will make all out efforts to achieve the targets set for the Twelfth Plan.
Recommendation (Para 9.3)
The Committee notes that various ongoing projects/activities and proposed new initiatives
have been integrated into 15 broad major restructured programmes to carry out the research
activities in a more focused way. The Committee hopes that the new initiatives does not lead to
less focused monitoring or neglect of some of the programmes vis-a-vis the position existing so
far when these programmes were assigned individual budgetary allocations. The Committee,
therefore, recommends that the Ministry should carry out a review, after a suitable interval, to see
if the new system has helped/achieve/improved meeting of physical and financial targets and apprise
the Committee of the finding of such a review. The Committee would, however, like Ministry to
ensure that despite amalgamation of a large number of projects/schemes in a programme, individua1
focus and attention continues to be provided to each schemes and project of the Ministry.
Action Taken by Government
The Ministry would like to assure that all the ongoing and new schemes proposed for

4
implementation during Twelfth Plan would be implemented under the 15 Major umbrella schemes
without losing the focus of the individual activities. The necessary review mechanism has been in
place to monitor these activities separately.
Comments
The Committee is not satisfied with the reply furnished by the Ministry. The
Committee’s recommendation was meant for proper scrutiny and critical appraisal of new
monitoring mechanism.  The Committee therefore, reiterates that the Ministry should
immediately carry out the review of its activities/programmes to ascertain as to whether the
new system has worked as per expectation.
Recommendation (Para 10.4)
The Committee has always stressed upon the need for greater application of technologies
for socio-economic development of common masses. The Committee, therefore, commends the
initiative of the NIOT in using technology i.e. ‘Low Temperature Thermal Desalination (LTTD)’ to
solve the drinking water problem in two islands of Lakshadweep, by setting up two LTTD plants.
The Committee is also happy to know that NIOT, also proposed to set up six more plants in other
islands of Lakshadweep, through public-private partnership mode. The Committee is of the opinion
that such technologies needs to be popularized and such plants should also established in Andaman
& Nicobar Islands as well and other coastal regions of the country, which face a scarcity of fresh
drinking water. It also feels that the adoption of the public-private partnership model would make
the establishment of such plants more cost effective, and enable the Ministry to commission a
larger number of plants in the coastal regions of the country in a short time.
Action Taken by Government
Expressing gratitude to the Committee for appreciation, it is informed that the Ministry has
been making several efforts for popularizing the LTTD technology in selected coastal location and
island territories. NIOT has already taken steps to commission six more plants based on LTTD
technology in Lakhshadweep islands (Amini, Chetlet, Kadamath, Kalpeni, Kiltan and Andrott).
Efforts are underway to set up a LTTD plant with a capacity of generating two million litres of
freshwater per day (2 MLD) at Tuticorin.
Comments
The Committee hopes that proposed commissioning of six more LTTD plants in
Lakshdweep Islands and Tuticorin (Tamil Nadu), would be carried out as per schedule. The
Committee reiterates that technologies for the benefit of common man such as LTTD needs
to be encouraged and established in other coastal regions of the country like Andaman and
Nicobar Islands, which face a scarcity of fresh drinking water. It reiterates that the Ministry
may explore the public-private partnership model for setting up more such LTTD plants
which would make it more cost effective.
Recommendation (Para 10.8)
The Committee commends the efforts of the Ministry in augmenting the scientific and
technological capabilities of the INCOIS, in respect of predicting cyclones and tsunami, since
accurate and advance warnings about these natural hazards give sufficient time to disaster
management agencies to gear themselves better to minimize the loss of property and lives. The
Committee is also happy to note that the Indian Tsunami Warning System has been entrusted the

5
responsibility to, function as Regional Tsunami Service Provider by UNESCO and have started its
operation for the Indian Ocean Rim countries. The Committee commends the Ministry for making
accurate predictions on recent earthquake that hit certain parts of India and saving the country
from unnecessary anxiety and fear. The Committee appreciates the fact that the technological
capabilities of the INCOIS have been recognized internationally and hopes that, in future the Centre
would forge collaborations with similar scientific organizations of the advanced countries, to
provide ocean information and advisory services to society, industry, Government agencies and
scientific community through sustained ocean observations, information management, and focused
research.
Action Taken by Government
Thanking the Committee for the appreciation on work of augmentation of ocean information
services, it is mentioned that INCOIS would make every effort to forge cooperation with similar
similar scientific organizations of the advance countries, when ever required to provide best
possible ocean advisory services.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
Recommendation (Para 10.14)
The Committee notes the importance of the useful research being done by the IITM and
hopes that the Institute would successfully provide research backup needed for raising the
accuracy levels of our weather and climate forecasts to the highest international standards well
before the end of Twelfth Five Year Plan and the Committee recommends adequate budgetary
support during the period be provided to the Institute to achieve this task.
Action Taken by Government
The Ministry highly appreciates the recommendations of the Committee for the adequate
budgetary support to be provided to achieve the task of providing the research backup needed for
raising the accuracy levels of our weather and climate forecasts to the highest international
standards well before the end of Twelfth Five Year Plan. Some of the major actions taken towards
achieving the targets are (i) establishment of capacity to make dynamical prediction of seasonal
mean monsoon using coupled model (ii) An empirical system to predict the active and break spells
3-4 weeks in advance has also been developed. The High Performance Computer (RPC) of 70
Teraflop acquired by the HTM during the Eleventh Five Year Plan has provided great opportunity
for R&D that has gone in to the improvement in modeling work for weather and climate forecasts.
In order to work out a Modeling Framework and put it in use to predict seasonal mean climate
in India the Ministry has launched a Monsoon Mission with a view to design a weather prediction
model for improving the Indian monsoon weather and climate forecasts, ultimately to develop an
Indian Model (based on changes made to the CFS model) which will have the capability to better
simulate and predict the monsoon rainfall. High priority has been accorded to the development of
climate models for more reliable projection of climate change in the 21 st century – with a special
focus on the behaviour (frequency and intensity) of extreme events (heat waves, cold spells, severe
thunder storms, tropical cyclones, storm surges, severe storms, droughts, etc.) in the near future.
The development of a coupled modeling strategy as well as to generate a large ensemble of future
climate change scenarios using a suite of global and high resolution regional climate models
involves a large number crunching capability.

6
Comments
The Committee appreciates the efforts and the progress made by the Ministry for
improving accuracy of weather and climate predictions. It also notes that the Ministry has
launched ‘Monsoon Mission’ a weather prediction model for better simulation and prediction
of the monsoon rainfall. The Committee hopes that efforts would also be made to pass on
the crucial cyclonic predictions/early warnings to the common man so as to avert any loss
of life and property.
Recommendation (Para 10.11)
The Committee is aware of National Centre for Antarctic and Ocean Research’s (NCAOR)
good performance in conducting scientific expeditions to Polar Regions. The Committee hopes
results of scientific studies being done in .Polar Regions would find useful application in glaciers
of Himalayas, forecasts and control relating to monsoons and in other areas and a better
understanding of climate change would emerge from these studies.
Action Taken by Government
Expressing gratitude to the Committee for the appreciation on scientific performance in
Polar Regions, it may be noted that the results of the scientific studies conducted in the Polar
Regions and the expertise gained out of it is planned to be extended to the Himalayan Glaciers
during the Twelfth Five Year Plan. NCAOR has initiated a long term programme on ‘Cryosphere
studies in Himalayas’ which is intended to conduct Ground Penetrating Radar (GPR) traverse,
studies on Snow and Ice Chemistry and Glacier dynan1ics of selected glaciers to begin with. This
would help us in better understanding of the impact of the climate change on the Himalayan Glaciers.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
Recommendation (Para 11.20)
The Committee, is of the opinion that research in the field of cloud physics should be
accorded high priority as it would not only help in right selection of clouds for seeding but would
help master its other aspects as well including development of cost effective techniques for
successful cloud seeding, which may go a long way in helping the country solve the problems of
drought and water scarcity in certain parts of the country. Such research may also provide greater
insights in understanding the dynamics of global warming. The Committee, therefore, strongly
recommends that Ministry should make all our efforts to strengthen the special laboratory which
has been set up at Mahabaleshwar to study all kinds of clouds from precipitation point of view
so that cost effective techniques for artificial precipitation could be  developed and for that, if
needed, adequate funds should be made available.
Action Taken by Government
The Ministry expresses gratitude for the recommendations of the Committee for adequate
budgetary support towards strengthening the special laboratory at Mahabaleshwar for addressing
the issues relating to clouds to understand complex interactions between aerosols, clouds and
circulation. It may be noted that the construction of the laboratory will commence after the
monsoon season is over in the month of October, 2012 and expected to be completed by June,
2013. The High Altitude Cloud Physics Laboratory will house the state of art instruments for the
observations.

7
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and at the same time hopes that the construction of
the laboratory would have commenced and would be completed as per schedule.
Recommendation (Para 12.3)
The Committee is happy to note that allocations made for R&D activities of IMD and for
the programmes ‘Research, Training, Education and Outreach’ taken together are sufficient and
hopes that a strong research backup would be available for the Ministry to complete its various
programmes and achieve its objectives during the year 2011-12.
Action Taken by Government
Expressing thanks to the Committee for its appreciation for the activities being carried out
under the programme on “Research, Training, Education and Outreach”, it is informed that during
2011-12, the Ministry had taken several initiatives to support academic programmes, establishment
of national lab facilities, capacity building through opening of training schools, national and
international collaboration etc. These have helped in achieving the objectives of the various
programmes of the Ministry.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
Recommendation (Paras 13.5 and 13.6)
The Committee fully understands that though it may not humanly possible to completely
control the forces of nature like earthquake, yet through technological interventions the massive
destruction and financial losses it causes can certainly be minimized. The Committee, therefore,
feels that, intensive efforts towards scientific research are needed to fully understand the various
aspects of earthquakes, it is, therefore, imperative to establish a separate institutional mechanism
to effectively deal with earthquake related issues in the country, so as to minimize the damage in
future due to earthquakes.
The Committee also notes that presently, various aspects of seismology related research are
being carried out in a fragmented way by several research, academic, State and Central
Government institutions in the county. In view of the extreme killer and destructive potential of
earthquake as a natural phenomenon. the Committee fully endorses the proposal of the Ministry to
set up a separate research institute of the nature of ‘National Centre of Seismology’ which is
exclusively devoted to study of the mechanic of earthquakes, geo-tectonic movements and -all
other aspects of earthquake so as to avoid/minimize the losses of life and property, a field which
is yet to be mastered by the human mind.
Action Taken by Government
The Ministry is actively considering setting up a National Centre for Seismology (NCS) with
a view to conduct focused research in the area of seismology. It may be mentioned that issues
relating to preparation, circulation of Expenditure Finance Committee (EFC) document, finalization
of site/land/construction of building and modalities of setting up of NCS is under consideration.
Comments
The Committee hopes that the procedural aspects relating to setting up of the

8
“National Centre for Seismology’ would be expedited and the Centre established at the
earliest, for carrying out concerted research in the field of seismology, so as to minimize
loss of life and property caused due to earthquakes.
Recommendation (Paras 14.7 and 14.8)
The Committee is of the opinion that the agricultural economy of the country is immensely
affected by the vagaries of nature. However, this effect can on]y be minimized with scientific
inputs, through the installation of state-of-the-art weather observation system throughout the
country and utilizing them for providing accurate and advance information to the farmers pertaining
to the weather and climatic conditions. In this connection the Committee appreciates the Ministry
for initiating the ‘Agro-meteorological services’ to provide advance information to the farmers
pertaining to wind, temperature, rainfall, humidity and soil moisture and help them to plan the
cultivation and harvesting of various crops and in issuing district-level bulletins to 560 districts
across the country. The Committee notes with satisfaction that the Government intends to increase
the coverage of farmers under the agro-meteorological services from the current level of 10% to
around 40%.
The Committee recommends that the Ministry should develop Atmospheric Observations
Systems Network and Atmospheric Processes & Modeling and Services throughout the country in
a time bound manner so as to improve weather and climate forecasting services. The Committee
further recommends that agro-meteorological advisory services should be extended to cover all
districts of the country. The Committee further recommends that crop and location specific
information to farmers be disseminated in a more friendly manner and its reach extended to cover
all farmers in a time-bound manner, so that even small and marginal farmers could full benefit of
these services.
Action Taken by Government
Expressing the gratitude to the Committee, the Ministry would like to inform that at present
127 Agro-Automatic Weather stations have been installed to issue more accurate advisories to the
farmers. In addition to that, Automatic Weather Station recently installed at various locations are
also used for the same. The observations from these automatic weather stations are extensively
used in the preparation of crop and location specific advisories for the farmers. Implementations
of various programmes, popularization of the Agromet Services are being made to outreach these
services to the maximum number of farmers in the country. Efforts will be made to increase user
network of this service.
Under the modernization programme of IMD, efforts are being made to improve the
forecasting system by installation of more weather observations and introduction of different high
resolution indigenous and other models available in different parts of the world. For improving the
outreach of the advisories, the same are sent through SMS and IVRS mode to the farmers in
different States in PPP mode. The advisories will also be disseminated on line through the Farmers’
Club under the network of National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD). Apart
from these, advisories are also disseminated using already existing channels like internet, print
media, Door Darshan Kendras, AIR and other cable TV networks to communicate the Agromet
Advisories to the huge number of farmer in a user friendly manner. IMD shall provide any support
if required for full implementation of the recommendations.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.

9
Recommendation (Para 15.3)
The Committee appreciates the good initiative of the Ministry in providing the fishermen
advance advisories, which have led to reduction of search time and increase in the catch per unit
effort, resulting in an increased net profit from 1.5 to 2.5 times and fuel savings upto 30%. The
Committee also note the proposal to increase the user base of these advisories from the existing
65% to 90% of the fishermen across the country, by the end of the Plan period. The Committee
desires the Ministry to make concerted efforts to achieve this target.
Action Taken by Government
Expressing the gratitude to the Committee for the appreciation on fisherman advisory
services, the Ministry will make every effort to augment user base of the Potential Fishery zone
advisories and to reach out fisherman community.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and hopes that the Ministry would be able to achieve
its objective of increasing the user base from the existing 65% to 90% of the fishermen
who are beneficiaries of these advisories, by the end of the Plan period.
Recommendation (Para 16.2)
The Committee feels that there is an urgent need for making concerted efforts to improve
the accuracy of out weather and climate services. In a country like India, where a large section
of population is dependent on agriculture for its living, correct and reliable weather prediction well
in advance, will prove a boon for the farmers. The Committee, therefore, feels that instead of
putting a distant plan of achieving the United States level of accuracy, in climate and weather
forecasting in the next five years, the Ministry should make all out efforts to improve our weather
and climate prediction services and bring them at par with the highest international standards of
accuracy within the next three years.
Action Taken by Government
Towards this, a five day district level Medium Range Weather Forecast is being issued since
June, 2008. During recent years, there is considerable improvement in quality of the forecast
issued. Continuous efforts are being made for improvement of the quality of these forecasts to
bring them at par with the highest international standards or accuracy. During Twelfth Five Year
Plan, it is also proposed to develop and issue block level Medium Range Weather Forecast for
facilitating the preparation of block level Agromet advisories as per the need of the marginal and
small farmers.
Comments
The Committee hopes that the proposal for the development and issue of block level
Medium Range Weather Forecast, to facilitate the preparation of block level Agromet
advisory services would be pursued and completed as per schedule, keeping in mind the
benefits that would accrue to the marginal and small farmers.
Recommendation (Para 17.5)
The Committee acknowledges the significance of the Indian polar missions as the climatic
conditions in these regions have a direct bearing on the monsoons, which is the lifeline of the

10
agriculture in our country. The Committee commends the setting of the Indian polar stations which
would increase the base of data collection regarding polar processes. The Committee hopes that
Bharati station would be commissioned as per schedule and start its operations during the year
2012-13, which will give significant boost to India’s polar research programme. The Committee
recommends that the continuing long term approved scientific projects which are the proposed
activity under the “Polar Science and Cryosphere” should be pursued diligently and in a well-
planned and strategic manner and the data collected from its scientific expeditions must be analyzed
and a serious endeavor made to use the results to predict the Indian monsoons more accurately.
Action Taken by Government
Thanking the Committee for appreciating the setting up of new Indian Station’ Bharati’ in
Antarctica, it is informed that the station has since been operationalised and first team has already
commenced wintering in the station. The collection of scientific data on weather parameter and
Geomagnetic Observation has already commenced.
Comments
The Committee congratulates the Ministry for the operationalisation of the new
Indian Station ‘Bharati’ and hopes that India’s polar research programme would reach new
heights and would help in the accurate prediction of the Indian monsoons.
Recommendation (Para 18.4)
The Committee, notes with concern that there was a shortfall in utilization of allocated funds
by the Ministry, to the tune of Rs.1.24 crores in the year 2009-10 and Rs.2.54 crores in the year
2010-11; which is evident from the difference in B.E. and Actual allocations for the said years. The
shortfall in utilization, is even more apparent for the year 2012, where the B.E. allocation stood
reduced from Rs.18.00 crores to Rs.2.00 crores only, i.e. a drastic reduction of about 90 per cent
of allocated budget. The Committee takes a serious view of the under utilization of funds in last few
years by the Ministry, which shows that the Ministry is not seriously pursuing this important
programme viz.. Polymetallic Nodules Programme. The Committee, therefore, strongly recommends
that the Ministry must actively pursue this programme and the programme must be carried forward
with full vigour, for exploitation of the mineral resources in our vast Exclusive Economic Zone to
enhance availability of sufficient mineral resources required for our industrial growth.
Action Taken by Government
Recognizing the past financial performance of the programme, the Ministry has taken up
advance action to identify for chartering of a research vessel towards conducting topographic
survey of EEZ. Another partner has been identified to accelerate the work. The drastic under
utilizations of funds particularly during the year 2011-12 could be due to non-availability of required
chartered research vessel.
Comments
The Committee feels that the procedural requirements such as requirement of
chartered research vessel, ought to be sorted out without any further delay and the funds
allocated for the purpose must be utilized meticulously.
Recommendation (Para 19.4)
The Committee observes that as regards the detection and quantification of  gas-hydrates,

11
major portions of  the deep-water regions have remained unexplored and available data is inadequate
for the assessment of  gas-hydrates. The Committee therefore recommends that evaluation and
quantification of  gas-hydrates must be intensified in the EEZ region of  the country to fully explore
this resource especially in view of  its potential as clean fuel resource. The Committee is of  the
opinion that to meet the ever increasing demand of  energy in the country, it is imperative to explore
alternate sources of  energy as soon as possible and therefore such programmes should be actively
pursued and adequately funded.
Action Taken by Government
Ministry is already working on developing technologies for exploration. The Autonomous
Coring system has been developed and trials are continuing. Similarly remotely operated submersible
has been developed for exploration of  gas hydrates. Presently there is no technology available for
extraction of  gas hydrates from deep waters.
Comments
The Committee notes the efforts of  the Ministry and reiterates that the exploration
of gas hydrates should be expedited to meet the ever increasing demand for energy.
