The Department accepts the recommendation and assures the committee of maximum
utilization of the fund allocated to the Department. Secretary, DST reviews the plan budget/
expenditure every month to ensure maximum utilisation of allocated resources.
Though there are several new programmes that have been planned for the Twelfth Five year
Plan, the same could not be initiated due to many reasons including the advisory of Ministry
Finance to defer implementing new schemes. The Department has noted the observations of the
Standing Committee and would strengthen monitoring mechanisms and make it more robust to
ensure full and effective utilization of allocated funds.
Comments
The Committee takes note of the reply of the Department
Recommendation (Para 6.3)
The Committee feels that such cuts would lead to shortage of resources and may adversely
affect the progress of some of the programmes. The Committee further, notes that these disturbing
cuts have been imposed when new Science, Technology and Innovation Policy, 2013 has been
launched with much fanfare. While on one hand, the Government has given a healthy sign of
promoting science and innovations in the country but on the other hand it had not shown faith on
the scientific Departments like DST by imposing cuts on its proposed allocations. The Committee,
therefore, recommends that adequate funds should be made available to the Department at RE stage
by Planning Commission based on its requirements.
Action Taken by Government
The Department values the concerns raised by the committee for allocation of adequate
resources at RE stage. The Department has been prioritizing its programme based on the resources
available at the RE stage and would strive hard to utilize it to the fullest extent.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.

3
Recommendation (Para 7.10)
The Committee recommends that the key goals enshrined in the Policy document should be
realized within the given time frame particularly the goal of positioning India amongst the top five
global scientific powers by 2020 and the Department must make all out efforts to achieve these goals.
Action Taken by Government
The Department will make sincere efforts to achieve the goals enshrined in the Policy
document. A Policy Research Cell in this regard has already started functioning within the
Department. At least 4-5 Policy Research Centers, in the public-funded academic institutions will
be established to carry out policy related research in the remaining period of the Twelfth Plan.
Comments
The Committee takes note of setting up of Policy Research Cell but feels that the
Department should make sincere and focused efforts to realise the goals set in the Science,
Technology and Innovation Policy, 2013.
Recommendation (Para 9.5)
The Committee finds that Science and Engineering Research Board (SERB) has been formed
after taking into consideration the best practices and funding models of developed countries
including National Science Foundation of USA while adopting a research model which is suited to
Indian setting. The Committee while noting that research proposals for competitive grants are
subjected to two levels of appraisals expects that the Department shall implement the Basic
Research Programme efficiently based on the principles of transparency, impartiality and ethical
considerations to raise the standards of Basic research in the country.
Action Taken by Government
As observed by the Committee, the Science and Engineering Research Board (SERB) has
instituted various appraisal levels to implement the Basic Research Programme efficiently based on
the principles of transparency, impartiality and ethical considerations to raise the standards of basic
research in the country.
Comments
The Committee appreciates that the Science and Engineering Research Board (SERB)
has instituted various appraisal levels to implement the Basic Research Programme
efficiently and hopes appraisals would be made objectively and in a purposeful manner and
steps taken by the Department would lead to raising the standards of basic research in the
country.
Recommendation (Para 10.11)
The Committee feels that in order to enhance investment in R&D, the private sector’s
contribution needs to be significantly augmented. The Committee had in its 223
rd report emphasized
on the need to enhance private sector contribution to R&D by offering incentives, forming
partnership, etc. The Department in their Action Taken Replies endorsed the view of the Committee
but the desired result still eludes us. The Committee feels that somewhere we have failed in our
efforts to woo private sector and not much has been achieved even in the second year of the
Twelfth Five Year Plan period.

4
Action Taken by Government
It is an undisputed fact that if India were to achieve the goal of 2% of GDP expenditure
on R&D, private sector investment into R&D needs to be significantly augmented. This issue has
also been highlighted by the Government during formulation of Twelfth Five Year Plan.
At present, the Government is providing various indirect tax incentives to the private sector
for R&D. Some of these incentives are – 100% write off of revenue expenditure on R&D; 100%
write off of capital expenditure on R&D in the year the expenditure is incurred; weighted tax
deduction @200% for sponsored research programmes in approved national laboratories,
Universities and IITs; weighted tax deduction @ 200% on in-house R&D expenditure to companies
engaged in the business of bio-technology or in the business of manufacture or production of any
article or thing not being an article or thing specified in the list of the eleventh schedule; income-
tax exemption @175% to donations made to approved non commercial scientific and industrial
research organizations; accelerated depreciation allowance for investment in plant and machinery
based on indigenous technology. Similarly, exemptions from Customs and Central Excise duty are
available in various forms to private sector. Various types of direct incentives are also provided to
the private sector in the form of grant/loan by Department of Science and Technology, Department
of Scientific and Industrial Research, Department of Biotechnology.
A Joint Committee of Industry and Government has been constituted by the Department of
Science and Technology in 2011 to look into various aspects related to stimulation of investment
of private sector into R&D in India. The Committee has pointed out that current estimates of
private sector investment into R&D is generally limited to those incurred for direct research in a
laboratory in the form of plant and machinery, manpower, consumables and utilities and they do
not cover costs relating to translation of R&D like test-beds, design and development,
standardization, field costs, etc. The Committee was of the view that current investment of private
sector into R&D might be underestimated and the estimate may not capture all investments being
made by the non-government sector in India.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and hopes that the Department will take steps to get
investment of private sector into R&D estimated as per international norms and in case
these estimates show lower levels of private sector investment, the Department should take
steps to find out reasons as to why private sector investments into R&D are low in India
vis-à-vis investment in other developed countries despite various concessions available and
work out a potent strategy to stimulate private sector investment into R&D in India.
Recommendation (Para 10.12)
The Committee recommends that Ministry must devise innovative ways to substantially
increase private sector investment in R&D in order to make it at par with the investment of private
sector in R&D as in other developed countries. The Government may even consider making
contribution of the private sector in R&D mandatory taking a cue from South Korean experience
which reversed South Korean Government’s burden in Science and technology Sector in a decade
with a series of laws. The Committee, further, recommends that Government should, in all
situations ensure that investment in R&D gets enhanced to at least 2% of Gross Domestic Product
at the earliest so as to realize the goal of becoming a scientific super power by 2020.
Action Taken by Government
The Department is proactively working towards stimulation of investment of private sector
into R&D through various ways. The suggestion of the Committee to consider making contribution

5
of private sector in R&D mandatory may need wider consultation with the stakeholders at all levels
Government and private sector, and a consensus needs to be arrived at political level before a law
is considered to be passed by the Government in this regard. The best course would be to motivate
the private sector in increasing their share of investment into R&D voluntarily in view of the
benefits it would bring to the private sector in terms of global competitiveness.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and hopes that further steps would be taken to
generate new sources of R&D funding and motivate private Sector to invest more in R&D.
Recommendation (Para 11.10)
The Committee takes note of considerable improvement in the performance of some major
universities in their contribution to research and publications. The Committee is, however, of the
view that we shall have to put in tremendous efforts to make the quality of teaching and research
in our Institutions and Universities at par with the best in the world. The Committee, therefore,
recommends that the Department should provide greater focus on the quality of teaching and
research in our Institutions and Universities.
Action Taken by Government
As observed by the Committee, there is considerable improvement in the performance of
Universities in respect of research and publications due to implementation of a few ongoing
Schemes like ‘Funds for Improvement of S&T Infrastructure in Universities and Higher Educational
Institutions’ (FIST) as well as initiation of a few new schemes in 11th plan like ‘Promotion of
University Research and Scientific Excellence’ (PURSE), “Consolidation of University Research for
Innovation and Excellence (CURIE) in Women Universities”, Special Package for North East Region
(NER), Jammu and Kashmir and Bihar. In the 12th Plan, all these ongoing efforts have been
strengthened by enlarging the Scope of Support and a greater focus towards improving the quality
both in teaching and research to a large number of institutions.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply. The reply of the Department is, however, silent on
whether the measures taken by the Department has resulted in improved quality of
teaching and research in our institutions and universities. The Committee notes with
unhappiness that despite the various measures taken by the Department, India has only
four institutions to the top 400 list and top most Indian university was placed between 226
and 250 in the global rankings. India’s prestigious Indian Institute of Technology (IITs),
were ranked in the 351-400 bracket. The Department needs to take effective measures to
improve the quality of teaching and Research in our institutions and Universities.
Recommendation (Para 11.11)
In addition, the Committee also recommends that the Department should also provide support
to improve the quality of research and teaching in the universities/Higher education Institutions based
in backward and far-flung, remote areas of the country and bring them at par with Research
Institutions/Research Laboratories of the country by the end of Twelfth Five Year Plan.
Action Taken by Government
The ongoing schemes like ‘FIST’ and Special Packages for North-East Region, Jammu and
Kashmir and Bihar are already in place to take care of strengthening infrastructure facilities at the

6
less-endowed institutes including Colleges, institutes located in remote places such as North-eastern
region, Jammu and Kashmir and Bihar State etc. While there has been a considerable impact of all
these schemes in respect of increase in publications etc., from these institutions, plans have already
been initiated in the XII Plan to widen the scope under these schemes so that more institutions
could be covered with the aim to bring them at par with other institutions in the country.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply. The Committee, however, would like the Department
to make an assessment as to the extent the measures taken by it have helped at the
ground level to improve the quality of research and teaching in the Universities in
backward, far-flung and remote areas of the country.
Recommendation (Para 12.5)
The Committee feels that in a country such as ours, where a large section of the population
lives in abject poverty, technological achievements made in the laboratories would be more valuable
if these also address the cause of the underprivileged masses and help in alleviating their poverty.
In this context, the Committee appreciates the programme undertaken by the Department for
livelihood generation and improving the quality of life of people at large particularly the scheduled
castes and scheduled tribes by providing affordable technology solutions and other scientific
interventions.
Recommendation (Para 12.6)
The Committee, however, would like to see such benefits extended further to cover more
and more scheduled castes and scheduled tribes’ population and accordingly, recommends that the
Department should further expand this programme.
Action Taken by Government
As regards to the recommendations contained in Para Nos 12.5 and 12.6, the Committee
would be happy to know that a new programme under the name Technology Application for
Livelihood Improvement (TALIM) has been initiated to cover more and more vulnerable sections
of the Scheduled Caste population.
Comments
The Committee appreciates the new initiative taken by the Department to uplift
weaker segment of the Society through Technology Application for Livelihood Improvement
(TALIM) scheme and hopes that concrete results would flow in the near future from the
programmes launched by the Department. The Committee also expects that efforts of the
Department for livelihood generation and improving the quality of life of people would boost
the interest of socially weaker segments of the society in Science and Technology and help
to raise their standards of living.
Recommendation (Para 13.7)
The Committee notes that the Department is undertaking modernisation and upgradation of
infrastructure and technical capabilities of SoI and NATMO under the programme “Modernisation
of Mapping Organisations”. The Committee, however, notes that in the year 2012-13, Department
failed to fully utilize funds made available to it under this programme. Modernisation of

7
infrastructural facilities and upgradation of data capturing and processing capabilities and technical
skills of these organizations are essential for efficient exploration and mapping of the country’s
domain and to ensure that all resources available in the country contribute in their full measures
to the progress, prosperity and security of our country. The Committee, therefore, expresses its
displeasure that the Department has not even been able to fully utilize funds meant for upgradation
of infrastructure of its two important organisations and recommends that the Department should
take all necessary measures to ensure early and successful implementation of this programme.
Action Taken by Government
The recommendations made by the Committee have been accepted by both Survey of India
(SoI) and National Atlas and Thematic Mapping Organization (NATMO). Both the organizations are
taking necessary steps to implement the recommendations and to ensure that the funds allotted to
them in the financial year 2013-14 are fully utilized.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
Recommendation (Para 14.4)
The Committee notes that DISHA Programme has been launched by the Department to
encourage women to pursue a career in science research as also for augmenting the pool of
women scientists in the country and is a socially useful programme. The Department has funded
projects and provided scholarship to women scientists under this programme. The Committee,
further, notes that there has been a marginal increase in the funds allocated to the programme in
the current fiscal year and hopes that Department will make efficient use of funds allocated in a
transparent and objective manner so that objectives of the programme are achieved.
Action Taken by Government
In order to take the programme of ‘DISHA’ forward, the scheme has been modified to
enhance its outreach to all parts of the country. Another proposed modification is the provision for
one year internship of Women Scientists to facilitate collection of data by literature research,
baseline data and beneficiary requirement so that Women Scientist can generate a viable project
under the mentorship of senior scientists of the National Institutes.
Comments
The Committee takes note of the reply. The Committee would like the Department to carry
out periodic review of its schemes such as ‘DISHA’ and commission an independent study
to assess the actual benefits flowing from its schemes to bring gender parity in S&T
Research and Development.
Recommendation (Para 15.4)
The Committee commends the measures taken by the Department to attract and retain
Indian scientists who have settled in various parts of the world for pursuing research in India in
their respective field of expertise as well as in home country research programs and notes with
satisfaction that measures taken have led to reversal of flow of researchers. The Committee
recommends that further measures be taken to make career in science, research and innovation
lucrative enough to attract best talent available in the country.

8
Action Taken by Government
The Department has given special attention to bring back Indian brain to our country to
pursue world class research in Indian setting. The ongoing Ramanujan Fellowship of the
Department for brilliant scientists and engineers from all over the world to take up scientific
research positions in India has received utmost attention and the number of fellowships is
increasing steadily. Further, the Department has approved institution of National Jawaharlal Nehru
Science Fellowship aimed to attract scientists of global eminence to come and work in Indian
Academic and Research Institutions. These measures make career in science, research and
innovation lucrative enough to attract best talent available in the country.
As recommended by the Parliamentary Standing Committee further measure are being taken
by DST to make career in Science, research and innovation lucrative enough to attract best talent
available in the country. International Division facilitates synergies of national S&T initiatives by
contributing in building suitable recommendations under the frameworks of:
● PM Global Advisory Council of Overseas Indians (PM GAC-OI) and its associated
Steering Group on Knowledge transfer, Science and Technology and Higher Education Collaboration
and Ministry of Overseas Indian Affairs focuses on drawing upon the experience, knowledge and
skills of eminent people of Indian Origin in diverse fields.
● Ministry of Overseas Indian Affairs sponsored “Global Indian Network of Knowledge
(Global INK)”, an electronic platform for harnessing the knowledge and skills of the Diaspora for
the benefit of the country; drawing on the knowledge and expertise of Global Indians, and of
people with an affinity for India, who are outstanding in areas of Environment, Healthcare,
Innovation and Science and Technology, without relocating them.
Apart from the ongoing Ramanujan Fellowship etc., during Eleventh Plan Period, the
Department of Science and Technology initiated a new scheme titled Innovation in Science Pursuit
for Inspired Research (INSPIRE) Faculty Award under ‘Assured Opportunity for Research Career
(AORC)’. Though this scheme is primarily designed for arresting the exodus of young talents from
India, it also attracts and brings back young scientists settled abroad. INSPIRE Faculty Award has
already been offered to about 100 young scientists engaged in research outside India for carrying
out research at the Indian Universities/Institutions.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and expects that initiatives taken by the Department
would bring the eminent Indian Scientists doing research abroad back to the country. The
Committee, however, would like the Department to assess as to the extent its initiatives
have led scholars of eminence to come back and work in the country.
Recommendation (Para 16.8)
The Committee feels that the Super Computing Facility and Capacity Building and National
Geographic Information System (NGIS) programmes are of great national importance and hence
recommends that the Department should make every possible effort to successfully implement them
in a time bound manner. The Committee, further, recommends that the Department must ensure
that the allocated outlays for these two schemes are fully utilized.
Action Taken by Government
The Department would take all necessarily steps for implementation of the Scheme Super
Computing Facility and Capacity Building ; thereby ensure the utilization of allocated outlays.

9
Department of Science and Technology (DST) and Department of Electronics and
Information Technology (Deity) are jointly implementing the project of Super Computing Facility
and Capacity Building. Deity has constituted a Committee to finalize the Expenditure Finance
Commission (EFC) document.
The modalities for positioning of National Geographic Information System (NGIS) have
been discussed in the High Power Governing Council meeting. The Expenditure Finance Committee
has also recommended the NGIS project. DST is in the process of obtaining the approval of the
Cabinet for selection of Mission Director on search-cum-selection basis.
Comments
The Committee notes that procedural requirements for the setting up of these two
new programmes, such as preparation of detailed project Report, approval through
Expenditure Finance Committee and Cabinet, appointment of a full time Mission Director
etc. has been initiated.
The Committee hopes that all the further necessary proposals to take these
programmes forward would be finalized expeditiously.
Recommendation (Para 17)
The Committee hopes that Department of Science and Technology shall make prudent
utilization of funds allocated to it under Demand No. 85 for the year 2013-14 having due regard
to the recommendations made by the Committee and efficiently implement its various programmes
and schemes in the year 2013-14.
Action Taken by Government
The recommendations of the Committee is noted for prudent utilization of allocated
resources by the Department during the year 2013-14.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.

REPORT
The Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Ministry of Environment
and Forests on the recommendations contained in the Two Hundred and Forty First Report of the
Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Science and Technology, Environment and
Forests on the Demands for Grants (2013-14) of the Ministry of Environment and Forests, which
was presented to both the Houses of Parliament on 8th May, 2013. The Committee had made a
total of twenty four recommendations/ observations which called for Action Taken Notes on the
part of the Ministry. Action Taken Notes on the report were received by the Committee on
13
th November, 2013. The Committee, on examination of Action Taken Notes, however is not
satisfied with action taken by the Ministry in respect of eleven recommendations/
observations and would like the Ministry to take further action in respect of such
recommendations as indicated in the Report.
The Committee’s recommendations, action taken thereon and comments of the Committee
on the Action Taken by the Ministry of Environment and Forests are set out in the subsequent
paragraphs:–
Recommendation (Para 7.2)
When the Committee enquired from the Ministry about the achievements in respect of the
above targets, the Ministry did not come out with specific and pointed reply. Going through the
replies, it is very difficult to make out precisely the physical achievements. In reply to the targets
of increasing forest and tree cover by 5 percentage points, the Ministry replied that in order to
achieve the target of 5 per cent, an additional 16.5 million hectares forest and tree cover had to
be obtained by 2012. But the tree planting during the Plan period was around 1.52 million hectare
per year which if multiplied by 5, gives a figure of 7.6 million hectares during the Plan period,
thus showing an overall shortage of plantation in 8.9 million hectares. The Ministry further stated
that given the constraints of land and financial resources, the achievement of the target was
ambitious. With regard to the target of treating all urban waste water by 2011-12 in order to clean
river waters, the Ministry stated that the primary responsibility of treating sewage was with the
Municipalities. The Ministry further added that maintaining cleanliness of rivers required minimum
river water and it was the Ministry of Water Resources, which was the nodal Ministry to ensure
adequate water flow in rivers. The Ministry thus had limited role to play in achievement of this
target. On the target of attaining World Health Organisation standards of Air Quality in all major
cities by 2011-12, the Ministry had a very peculiar reply to offer. The Ministry felt that the notified
National Ambient Air Quality Standards in India, based mostly on United States Environmental
Protection Agency health Criteria (USEPA) documents and not WHO Guidelines which provide a
more realistic and appropriate goal for achieving better air quality in India. Responding to the
monitorable target of enhancing energy efficiency by 20 per cent points by 2016-17. The Ministry
tossed the ball in the court of the Ministry of Power stating that action on enhancement of energy
efficiency and lowering energy intensity was the responsibility of Ministry of Power. The
Committee feels that if the Ministry has to handle the socio-economic monitorable targets given to
it in such a casual and cavalier manner, the very purpose of devising and deciding a target becomes
meaningless. The Ministry should have, while or before fixing the target, thought as to whether
the targets pertained to it or not. But once the targets were set, the Ministry must have made
sincere and serious efforts to meet them in close coordination and cooperation with the other
concerned Ministries. The Committee takes a very serious view on the way and the manner in
which the targets given to the Ministry had been handled. The Committee feels that if the Ministry
was not serious in trying to seriously pursue the targets set, they must not have accepted these

2
monitorable targets at all. The Committee hopes that monitorable socio-economic targets set for the
Twelfth Five Year Plan would not meet the same fate as the targets of the Eleventh Five Year Plan
and therefore, recommends, that the Ministry should seriously and vigorously pursue the targets
and goals set for the Twelfth Five Year Plan and ensure that concrete achievements in respect of
each target are made.
Action taken by Government
No reply has been given.
Comments (Para 7.2)
The Committee is constrained to observe that the Ministry has not sincerely and seriously
studied the report of the Committee as a result of which it has failed to give action taken reply
to the recommendation made in the paragraph. It is also likely that the Ministry has tried to brush
the uncomfortable and hard-hitting observations of the Committee under the carpet. Whatever the
fact of the matter, the Committee takes a very serious view of such a casual approach of the
Ministry towards the recommendation of the Committee and desires that the Ministry would be
more careful in future. The Committee, therefore, reiterates its recommendation that the
Ministry should seriously and vigorously pursue the targets and goals, so as to ensure that
concrete achievements in respect of each target are made and the repeat of the monitorable
socio-economic targets set in the mid-term appraisal document of the Planning Commission
for the Eleventh Five Year Plan period is obviated.
Recommendation (Para 8.1)
The Ministry was provided an outlay of R10,000.00 crores in the Eleventh Five Year Plan
(2007-12), out of which Environment and Ecology accounted for R3786.01 crores and Forestry
and Wildlife R6213.99 crores. Sector-wise distribution was R1246.01 crores for Environment;
R2540.00 crores for National River Conservation Directorate (NRCD); R2943.99 crores for Forests
and Wildlife; R3150.00 Crores for National Afforestation and Eco-Development Board (NAEB) and
R12.00 crores for Animal Welfare. However, by the end of the Plan period, the actual outlay, based
on year-wise allocation remained at R9231.00 crores with sectoral share of R1913.34 crores;
R2760.75 crores; R2611.44 crores; R1826.47 crores and R119.00 crores for Environment; NRCD;
Forests and Wildlife; NAEB and Animal Welfare respectively. Environment and Ecology thus finally
accounted for R4674.09 crores and Forestry and Wildlife R4556.91 crores. While Environment and
Ecology got R888.08 crores more, Forestry and Wildlife got R1657.08 crores less than the initial
earmarking of Budgetary allocation. There was, however, a reduction of R769.54 crores in the
original outlay for the Eleventh Five Year Plan which got restricted to R9231.00 crores as against
R10000.00 crores. On a comparative analysis of the original/initial vis-a-vis actual Sector-wise
outlay, it is found that while National Afforestation and Eco-Development Board which consists of
the key programme of national afforestation was the worst sufferer, Forests and Wildlife was the
second worst sufferer in terms of reduction in allocation. As against an initial amount of
R3150.00 crores and R2943.99 crores, earmarked under these sectors, the final outlay came down
to R1826.47 crores and R2611.44 crores, showing a reduction of R1323.53 and R332.55 crores
respectively.

Recommendation (9.6)
The Committee expresses its deep anguish over the declining percentage of share for the
Ministry of Environment and Forests in the overall Central Plan outlay in the successive Five Year

4
Plans/Annual Plans despite increasing importance of environmental issues. The Committee takes
a very serious note of the fact that while in the Eleventh Five Year Plan, the percentage share
was 0.83 per cent, it has gone down by more than 50 per cent to 0.41 per cent in the Twelfth
Five Year Plan. The Committee is of the considered view that Planning Commission must not
consider Budgetary Support made to Environment and Forests as non-productive, non-priority
and hence avoidable. The Planning Commission needs to understand and realize that the damage
done to environment, disturbance made to the ecological balance can’t be easily repaired and
restored. It, therefore, becomes expedient that the very process of degradation and degeneration
of environmental resources be contained and minimized to the possible extent though preventive
and curative measures before it is too late and it is possible inter-alia by mounting environmental
surveillance and reinforcing monitoring mechanism – the task assigned to Ministry of
Environment and Forests. For doing all these sufficient monetary support is undoubtedly
required. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Planning Commission must act on its
own observation of allocating 5 per cent of the Annual Central Sector Outlay to Environment and
Forestry Sectors in right earnest. The Committee also recommends that Ministry of Environment
and Forests must not only forcefully and vigorously take up this matter with the Planning
Commission but also apprise it of the details of response gathered from the Planning Commission
in this regard. The Committee also recommends that the Planning Commission must ensure full
allocation of the approved outlay during the Twelfth Plan period and should not resort to any cut
at RE Stage in any of the Annual Plans unless Ministry itself is not in a position to utilise the
full allocation. In any case, full requirements of the Ministry of Environment and Forests must
be met. The Ministry must, at the same time, make all out efforts to make full utilisation of
allocated budgetary outlay so as not to provide any alibi to the Planning Commission for
reduction at RE Stage.
Action Taken by Government
The recommendations of the Committee have been forwarded to the Planning Commission
with the request to actively consider allocating 5% of the Annual Central Sector Outlay to this
Ministry as observed by them, which is being vigorously pursued. The Planning Commission has
also been requested to ensure that the full requirements of this Ministry are met so that the
Ministry is able to fulfill its mandated tasks more effectively and efficiently. The Committee would
be apprised of the response of the Planning Commission as soon as it is received.
For the purpose of fuller utilization of allocated budgetary outlays, regular monitoring of
expenditure under various Schemes administered by the Ministry has been instituted at Divisional
Head level, with review of progress made at higher levels. This monitoring is carried out both at
Central Government as well as field levels. Besides, major Schemes of the Ministry also have an
in-built independent monitoring mechanism to ensure effective and timely utilisation of funds.
Electronic Clearance of funds for various Schemes/Projects has also contributed to quicker and
faster disbursement of funds. In addition, inclusion of the Ministry in Modified Cash Management
System w.e.f. 2012-13 has also facilitated better financial planning and proper and effective
utilisation of funds.
Comments (9.6)
The Committee notes the reply.
Recommendation (Para 10.6)
The Committee feels that this phenomenon of underutilization of allocated outlay is a very
serious matter towards which the Ministry needs to focus its attention in a more pragmatic and

5
professional manner and initiate concrete measures. Merely, reemphasizing and reiterating that the
Ministry has already in place a robust and sound monitoring mechanism would not do any good
particularly in view of the fact underutilization of allocated budgetary resources has turned out
to be a recurring phenomenon. It becomes all the more imperative, because underutilization of
allocated resources provides the Planning Commission and the Ministry of Finance with an alibi
to make less allocation in the next year and also allows them to use it as a tool to reduce the
approved BE outlay at the RE Stage. The Minister of Finance has made it amply clear in his
budget speech. The Ministry can justify its demand for additional resources only when it is able
to first utilise the entire resources allocated to it. The Committee, therefore, strongly
recommends that the Ministry of Environment and Forests must take sincere, serious and potent
efforts by way of meticulous planning, timely implementation and stricter monitoring of schemes/
projects and should not come out with the same lame and routine excuses for underutilization
year after year.
Action Taken by Government
The Ministry has taken up sincere, serious and potent efforts for ensuring maximum
utilisation of funds allocated to it covering all three aspects, namely, meticulous planning, timely
implementation and stricter monitoring. In conformance with the Modified Cash Management
System, Quarterly as well as Monthly Expenditure Plans (QEP/MEP) have been drawn up for each
Sub-Scheme. At the end of the first Quarter (April-June 2013-14), a detailed review has been
carried out and efforts intensified towards bridging any expenditure gap in any Sub-Scheme.
Monthly monitoring of progress made in timely implementation of each Sub-Scheme and meeting
the financial and physical targets has also been taken up. Apart from the tools already existing/
available for ensuring maximum utilisation of funds allocated to it, the Ministry also proposes to
require the Subject Divisions concerned to prepare a detailed schedule of expenditure against their
request/demand for grants well in advance of the following Financial Year. As a result of the
strengthened monitoring as well as review of progress of expenditures against the annual outlay of
R2,430/- crore in each of the two financial years (2012-13 and 2013-14) at BE stage, as of
31
st July, 2013 sanctions of expenditures across all Plan Schemes amounted to R672.06 crore,
resulting in a utilisation ratio of 27.66% which is significantly higher than expenditure amounting
to R458.80 crore or utilisation ratio of 18.80% achieved during the comparable period in the
previous year (as of 31
st July, 2012).
At the stage of finalisation of BE, the Subject Divisions would also be required to define
clear-cut and reasoned timelines according to which the schedule of expenditure vis-à-vis  the
finalised BE would be executed. In addition, executing agencies for the Plan Schemes would be
advised to take advance action with regard to submission of documents, including duly audited
Utilisation Certificates (UC) and Expenditure Statements (ES) along with requisite clearances/
approvals towards meeting the eligibility conditions for drawl of funds, so that the process of
expenditure could start immediately after allocation of grants, thereby minimising the timelag
between allocation of grants and actual incurring of expenditure. These strengthened efforts may
enable achievement of higher expenditures even when the actual outlay provided by the Planning
Commission falls short of the BE proposed by the Ministry as the Subject Divisions concerned
would have opportunity to raise expenditures further by the RE stage, thereby enabling placing
of demands for additional funds at RE stage for favourable consideration of the Planning
Commission.
Comments (Para 10.6)
The Committee notes the reply and hopes that the steps taken by the Ministry would
help address the perennial problem of underutilisation of allocated funds.

Observation (Para 13.2)
While the Committee takes note of the huge gap between availability of fund vis-à-vis its
requirement, it feels that the entire required funding cannot be done by the Government of India,
owing to budgetary constraints, although, it is of the considered view that volume of funding from
the Government of India must be reasonably raised. In such a situation, the Committee feels that
the Ministry should explore the possibilities of generating resources from sources other than the
Government of India. These sources could be managing loans from the Asian Development Bank
(ADB), the World Bank or the Japanese aid. Yet another source could be strict enforcement of
Polluters Pay Principle, so as to raise additional resources; making adequate provision for civil
administrative adjudication to fast track levy of penalty, etc. by making environment laws more
stringent and effective. Integrating environmental elements/factors into cost benefit analysis while
making public, as well as, private investment decisions for more prudent allocation of resources.
The Ministry may also think in terms of persuading Ministry of Finance to levy some green tax/
cess, on the lines of Education Cess/service tax, etc. The Ministry may also synergize its activities
with projects/programmes of those sectors of the economy which contribute to the volume of
pollution the most, i.e., the Transport Sector, Energy Sector, Oil Sector, Mining Sector, etc. and
require diversion of more forest land for non-forestry purposes. One such effort has been made
in Visakhapatnam, where the local public sector Units have voluntarily undertaken the task of
planting 40 lakh saplings in a span of five years and the progress of this experiment has been quite
satisfying. Such initiative can very well be replicated in other such cities/towns which are bearing

the compensatory afforestation fund having huge amount of money, i.e. , R1718.20 Crores
(Approx.) as principal amount as on 31
st March, 2012 and R384.59 Crores in the form of interest

Recommendation (Para 14.3)
The Committee understands The Companies Bill, 2012 mandates that any company having -
(i) net worth of R500.00 crores or more; (ii) turnover of R1000.00 crores or more; and
(iii) net profits of R5.00 crores or more in a financial year, shall spend at least 2 per cent of
average net profits of the last three years in pursuance of Company’s Corporate Social
Responsibility. The Bill further lists the activity which may be included by Companies in their
Corporate Social Responsibility Policies. Ensuring environmental sustainability has inter-alia been
included as one such permissible activity. The said Bill is yet to be passed by the Parliament. The
Committee recommends that Ministry of Environment and Forests may take up the matter with the
Ministry of Corporate Affairs for making necessary amendments in the Bill to particularly provide
for afforestation as an activity which could be undertaken under CSR and further to make it
mandatory that at least 50 per cent of the funds available for CSR shall be spent on afforestation.
By doing this, Ministry would be able to generate huge additional resources for massive
afforestation.
Action Taken by Government
The Ministry of Environment and Forests (MoEF) has been consistently pursuing both with
the Ministry of Corporate Affairs and Ministry of Heavy industries and Public enterprises, to make
provisions/guidelines to enhance the committed investment from CSR to 50% for massive tree
plantation in the interest of the welfare of our society.
Ministry has received response from Ministry of Corporate Affairs vide letter no 7/7/2011-
CL-I dated 8
th May, 2013, stating that the provisions on Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) have
been provided in the Companies Bill, 2012 under clause 135 read with Schedule VII of the Bill.
The said Bill has been passed by the Lok Sabha on 18.12.2012 and is awaiting approval of the
Rajya Sabha. The provisions of clause 135(CSR) shall be implementable after the Companies
Bill, 2012 is passed by both the Houses of Parliament, assented to by the President and notified
along with relevant rules.
As per latest observations of the Committee, MoEF has taken up the matter with Ministry
of Corporate affairs for making necessary amendments in the Companies Bill, 2012, and consider
bringing in a provision for earmarking 50% of the 2% CSR for afforestation and tree planting while
forming the CSR Guidelines.
Department of Public Enterprises has also been requested by MoEF to consider provisions
to enhance the committed investment from CSR to 50% in the area of afforestation and bring in
a proposal for cabinet approval to this effect, being the Nodal Department.

Recommendation (Para 15.7)
The Committee expresses its serious concern over the sorry state of affairs as regards
monitoring/reinforcement of forestry and environmental laws which has resulted in serious
environmental and ecological problems badly affecting the inhabitants of the nearby areas. Some of
the industrial clusters have become so polluted due to reckless and blatant discharge of effluents
and emissions that the residents are facing serious health hazards and even congenital problems.
If the situation is allowed to go as it is, a time will come when people would be forced to rise
against the proposed projects and hamper their progress. The Committee, therefore, is of the
opinion that the before the situation goes beyond control and takes ugly turn, the Ministry needs
to act in a serious and sincere manner. It, therefore, recommends that the proposals for enhancing
the number of regional offices of the Ministry and strengthening the existing ones should be
undertaken at the earliest, possibly during this financial year itself. The Committee also
recommends that the Planning Commission/Ministry of Finance should provide the Ministry with
adequate financial resources to enable the Ministry to achieve its desired objectives. The Committee
further recommends that apart from enhancing the number of regional offices and strengthening
them, the Ministry should consider further devolution of power and authority to the regional
offices.
